summary: The note describes a wave of youth-led activism demanding fiscal policy reforms to support sustainable development. It outlines their roadmap: green investment incentives, tax restructuring, environment-focused budgets, transparency, support for small businesses, infrastructure upgrades, education reform, and technology. It also stresses global cooperation with local action and intergenerational collaboration.
one_line: Youth activists push a fiscal reform roadmap, including green incentives, carbon-focused taxes, and transparent budgets, to build a sustainable economy.
key_facts: Discussions on overhauling traditional economic policies erupted after a watershed moment on September 1, 2023.
On October 12, 2023, 16-year-old climate advocate Emma González delivered a speech at the Youth Economic Forum calling for radical changes to fiscal policies.
Eleonora White, at 17, founded the organization "Green Futures Now," which orchestrated protests across major cities.
Activists urge recalibrating financial measures through tax credits, grants, or low-interest loans for green businesses, favoring renewable energy and eco-friendly technology.

Activists call for updated tax codes that penalize polluting industries and reward low-carbon alternatives; for Emma and her cohort, every percentage point increase in tax on fossil fuel giants is a step closer to carbon neutrality.
As the fiscal year begins in 2024, activists want budgets prioritizing environmental spending, including research into sustainable agriculture, clean transportation, and energy efficiency overhauls.
Activists demand clear publication of budget allocations and measurable environmental and social outcomes, with public and youth oversight of government spending.
Small businesses are seen as integral to the transition, to be empowered through subsidies and tailored tax breaks for eco-friendly operations.
Infrastructure demands include upgrading public transport, energy-efficient building codes, and broad-scale digitalization.
Emma González and allies argue reforms must be rooted in education, with curricula that intersect economy with ecology.
Technology such as blockchain for spending transparency and AI for predicting environmental impacts of fiscal measures is considered indispensable.

The activists advocate international cooperation while insisting local contexts guide policy application, and mentorship programs and joint task forces between seasoned economists and young activists are becoming common.
